sections.title: Overview
blocks: Facial ageing mixes **intrinsic** (genetics, time) and **extrinsic** (UV, smoking, pollution) change: volume loss, bone remodelling, elastosis and wrinkles. **Dynamic lines** appear with expression; **static lines** remain at rest.

This page is **counselling-level only** for community pharmacist IPs: what patients ask about neuromodulators and fillers, UK regulation, expected effects and red flags. It does **not** teach injection technique, doses, units or reconstitution.

ul: Dynamic lines: repeated frontalis, corrugator, orbicularis oculi and other facial muscle activity.
Static lines and folds: dermal thinning, fat-pad descent, bone resorption, gravity.
Botulinum toxin type A temporarily blocks acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction → reduced muscle contraction for about 3–4 months.
HA fillers restore volume by placing hyaluronic-acid gel in soft tissue — different products and planes (specialist detail).
Glabellar frown lines, forehead lines, crow’s feet are the common aesthetic requests.
Expected toxin timeline: onset over days, peak around 2 weeks, duration about 3–4 months.
Common local effects: bruising, short-lived headache, asymmetric smile if diffusion occurs.
Filler: immediate volume; swelling and bruising common early.

sections.title: Diagnosis and investigations
blocks: Aesthetic assessment belongs to a trained face-to-face prescriber. Community role: screen for skin-cancer lesions in photoaged faces before anyone treats pigment, and triage complications.

ddx.name: New facial asymmetry after toxin
ddx.f: Diffusion / brow or lid ptosis — usually temporary

ddx.name: Acute unilateral facial weakness with forehead spared
Painful livedo or blanching after filler
Descending paralysis, dysphagia after unlicensed injections

ul: Daily SPF, stop smoking, realistic expectations — toxin softens dynamic lines; it does not lift sagging skin or replace volume.
Botulinum toxin for cosmetic use is a **prescription-only medicine**. GPhC guidance: pharmacist prescribers must **examine face to face**; remote prescribing of these medicines is not appropriate.
Illegal under-18 cosmetic toxin/fillers (Botulinum Toxin and Cosmetic Fillers (Children) Act 2021).
Advise licensed UK product via a regulated, insured practitioner — never buy toxin online for self-injection.
Follow the treating clinician’s aftercare (often avoid rubbing, lying flat or vigorous exercise for the first hours).
Review at about 2 weeks rather than unplanned “top-ups”.
OTC “Botox-like” peptide creams have weak evidence — do not oversell.
Early: swelling, bruising, lumps. Delayed: nodules, biofilm infection — refer back to the injector/dermatology.
**Vascular occlusion:** severe pain, livedo, blanching soon after injection → **emergency** (injector/A&E; hyaluronidase is a specialist treatment).
**Visual loss / ophthalmoplegia after filler:** sight-threatening emergency — call 999; do not delay.

blocks.title: Unlicensed toxin / botulism
blocks.text: Descending weakness, dysarthria, dysphagia or breathing difficulty after aesthetic injections → 999. UKHSA may advise on antitoxin; notify health protection; Yellow Card. Check UK-licensed product and legitimate supply chain.

blocks.title: Therapeutic facial palsy toxin
blocks.text: Specialist facial-palsy teams use toxin for synkinesis and asymmetry alongside physiotherapy. Acute Bell’s palsy pathways (steroid within 72 h, eye protection) are separate — forehead-sparing weakness is stroke until proven otherwise.

refer.t: Visual symptoms or severe pain after filler → emergency.
Bilateral descending paralysis after unlicensed injections → 999 / UKHSA botulism pathway.
Drooping eyelid with corneal exposure risk → urgent eye care.

sections.title: Red flags and when to refer

ul: Visual symptoms or severe pain after filler → emergency.
Bilateral descending paralysis after unlicensed injections → 999 / UKHSA botulism pathway.
Drooping eyelid with corneal exposure risk → urgent eye care.
Stroke pattern facial weakness → 999.

pearls: This site intentionally omits units, dilution and injection maps — those belong in accredited aesthetic training, not a teaching website.
Photoaged faces need a skin-cancer check before cosmetic energy devices — see [photoageing](condition:photoageing) and [solar lentigines](condition:solar-lentigines).
Document advice and signpost legitimate practitioners; do not prescribe toxin remotely.
